title: Also show "Reformat or Edit in Partition Manager" action for removable storage devices with no mountable volumes
line: Disks & Devices now lists a USB stick that is blank or has no formatted partition, with a button that opens it in Partition Manager.
explanation: Disks & Devices only lists volumes it can open, plus drives matched by a Solid action. A stick with no partition table, or only partitions without a file system, has no such volume, and no action matches the drive itself, so the applet showed "No removable devices attached". Partition Manager's own "Reformat or Edit with Partition Manager" action only matches volumes that already have a file system. Now a removable drive with media is listed while none of its volumes are listed, with an "Open in Partition Manager" button that runs partitionmanager --device=/dev/sdX. The drive row is replaced by the volume as soon as a usable partition appears (e.g. after formatting), comes back when the partitions are deleted, and is only offered when Partition Manager is installed.

commits.message:
applets/devicenotifier: offer Partition Manager for unformatted drives

A USB stick that is blank or has no partition with a file system was
not listed at all, so there was no way to reformat it from the applet.
Such drives are now listed with a button that opens Partition Manager.

BUG: 460817

media.caption: Blank USB stick plugged in: Disks & Devices says no removable devices are attached
Same stick: it is listed with an Open in Partition Manager button
Clicking it opens Partition Manager on /dev/sdb (a stand-in window on the test rig)
Once formatted, the new volume replaces the drive; when its partitions are deleted, the drive comes back
